series.name: The Last Day
series.tagline: On this day, they were the biggest in the world. Tomorrow, they wouldn't exist.
series.concept: The final 24 hours of famous companies, empires, regimes, and cultural eras. What went wrong, who saw it coming, who was in denial. Each episode is a countdown to collapse.

episodes.title: Kodak — The Day Film Died

slides.text: 1996. 145,000 employees. $16 billion revenue. 90% of US film sales. 'Kodak Moment' in the dictionary.
1975. Kodak engineer built the first digital camera. Executives: 'No one wants pictures on a TV screen. Don't tell anyone.'
25 years of chances to lead digital. They had the patents, engineers, brand. But every digital camera meant one less film roll.
2000: Digital outsells film. 2008: iPhone launches with a camera. 2010: Instagram. Nobody needs Kodak.
January 19, 2012. Bankruptcy. 145,000 → 8,000 jobs. They saw the future. Didn't believe it.
They invented the digital camera and were too scared to follow it. The most dangerous place: top of the curve.

episodes.synopsis: Kodak invented digital camera in 1975. Buried it. Bankrupt by 2012.
episodes.caption: Kodak invented digital photography in 1975. Went bankrupt in 2012. Built the weapon that killed them. What company is doing this today?

episodes.title: Nokia — The Phone Everyone Forgot

slides.text: 2007. 437 million phones. Every other person had a Nokia. Then on June 29, a fruit company launched a glass rectangle.
Nokia on iPhone: 'No keyboard. No one will buy it.' The smirk that cost 50% of the global market.
Three failed OS in 5 years — Symbian, MeeGo, Windows Phone. Like switching engines mid-flight. While the plane is on fire.
2011. 'Burning Platform' memo. 'We must jump.' He jumped to Windows Phone. The platform was burning. He jumped into the ocean.
Sept 3, 2013. Microsoft buys Nokia's phone division. CEO in tears: 'We didn't do anything wrong, but we lost.'
Nokia thought 'phone' meant 'calls.' Apple knew it meant 'computer in your pocket.' Define the future or lose it.

episodes.synopsis: 50% global market. CEO cried: 'We didn't do anything wrong, but we lost.' iPhone erased Nokia.
episodes.caption: 50% market share. 437 million phones. 'Nobody wants a phone without buttons.' Nokia lost to imagination. What's next?

episodes.title: Lehman Brothers — The Day Wall Street Died

slides.text: 158 years old. Survived Civil War, two World Wars, Great Depression. $639 billion. Died from greed.
Bet everything on subprime mortgages. Lent to people who couldn't pay. Packaged garbage as gold. Until it caught fire.
Risk officers warned in 2006. Ignored. Demoted. One fired. When the problem-finder is punished, the problem becomes the company.
Sept 12-14. Emergency Fed meetings. Lehman begged for bailout. The answer: No.
Sept 15, 6:45 AM. Chapter 11. $639 billion — largest bankruptcy ever. Global markets crashed. Nobody went to jail.
When the person paid to warn you is silenced, you're already dead. You just don't know it yet.

episodes.synopsis: 158 years old. $639 billion in assets. September 15, 2008. Gone overnight.
episodes.caption: 158 years. Survived everything. Died from greed in 2 years. Nobody went to jail. Who's the next Lehman?

episodes.title: Blockbuster — Laughing at Netflix

slides.text: 9,000 stores. $6 billion revenue. Friday night ritual. Then a DVD-by-mail company knocked.
2000. Reed Hastings: 'Buy Netflix for $50M.' Antioco laughed. Most expensive laugh in business history.
$800M/year in late fees. Customers begged for change. Netflix: no late fees. Customers: goodbye.
Netflix streaming 2007. Blockbuster tries online 2008. Too late. Bankruptcy 2010. 9,000 stores → 1.
Netflix: $250 billion. Offered for $50M. One meeting. The future walked in the door and was laughed away.
Sometimes the future walks in your front door and you laugh it away.

episodes.synopsis: Netflix offered to sell for $50 million. Blockbuster laughed. Netflix: $250 billion. Last Blockbuster: tourist attraction.
episodes.caption: Netflix offered for $50M. Blockbuster laughed. Netflix: $250B. One Blockbuster remains — as a tourist attraction.

episodes.title: The Mughal Empire — The Richest Throne Falls

slides.text: 1700. 25% of global GDP. More than all of Europe combined. They built wonders while Europe fought over scraps.
After Aurangzeb, weak emperors. Marathas, Sikhs carved it up. In 50 years, 'Emperor' meant ruler of Delhi. Barely.
Bahadur Shah Zafar ruled nothing. British controlled everything. A prisoner with a crown, writing poetry.
1857. Sepoys asked Zafar to lead. He agreed. For months, he felt like an emperor. Then the British crushed it.
British killed his sons before him. Exiled to Rangoon. Died in a 4x8 room in 1862. Writing poetry about Delhi.
From 25% of GDP to a cell. Empires don't fall from outside. They hollow from within.

episodes.synopsis: 25% of global GDP. Last emperor died writing poetry in a cell in Rangoon.
episodes.caption: 25% of global GDP. Taj Mahal. Peacock Throne. Last emperor died in a 4x8 cell writing poetry. How the richest empire became nothing.

episodes.title: The Soviet Union — Christmas Collapse

slides.text: 22 million km². 8,000 nukes. First human in space. Terrified the West for 70 years. Simply stopped existing.
1980s bread lines. Empty shelves. Chernobyl. Couldn't buy jeans while building nuclear submarines.
Glasnost opened windows on a rotting building. People saw the rot. Then wanted to leave.
1989: Berlin Wall. 1990-91: 15 republics declared independence. Dissolving like sugar in tea.
December 25, 1991. 7:32 PM. Soviet flag lowered from Kremlin. Russian flag up. Signature and a flag change.
8,000 nukes couldn't save it. When people stop believing, no army can hold it together.

episodes.synopsis: 8,000 nukes. First to space. Ceased to exist on Christmas Day 1991.
episodes.caption: 8,000 nukes. First to space. Collapsed on Christmas 1991 without a shot. No empire is too big to fail.

episodes.title: Toys 'R' Us — Amazon Killed the Toy Store

slides.text: 'I don't want to grow up, I'm a Toys R Us kid.' 1,600 stores. $13 billion revenue. Temple of childhood.
Gave Amazon all their toy data for exclusive selling rights. Amazon broke the deal. Won the lawsuit. Lost the war.
Private equity loaded $5 billion in debt. $400M/year in interest. Not on toys — on debt.
Amazon + Walmart cheaper online. Why fight parking when you can click 'Buy Now' in pajamas?
June 29, 2018. 735 stores closed. Geoffrey photographed walking out with a suitcase. Internet cried.
Wasn't killed by Amazon alone. Killed by $5B in debt that left nothing for innovation.

episodes.synopsis: 1,600 stores. Killed by debt and Amazon. Geoffrey walked out with a suitcase.
episodes.caption: 1,600 stores. 33,000 jobs. Killed by debt and Amazon. The store where you dreamed is now a parking lot.

episodes.title: The Roman Empire — The Fall That Took 200 Years

slides.text: From Britain to Egypt. 70 million people. Roads, aqueducts, laws. Built civilization. Then stopped maintaining it.
26 emperors in 50 years — most murdered. Army chose emperors by highest bid. Leadership by assassination.
Debased currency. Mixed lead into silver. Prices rose 1,000% in a century. Your chai going from ₹10 to ₹10,000.
Goths, Vandals, Huns — didn't hate Rome. Wanted in. But walls crumbling, army tired, treasury empty.
September 4, 476 AD. A teenager surrendered the crown to a barbarian. 'Give me the crown.' And the boy did.
Corruption → Inflation → Division → Fall. Every time. The pattern doesn't change.

episodes.synopsis: 5 million km². 70 million people. Fell to corruption, inflation, and leaders who forgot the people.
episodes.caption: 5 million km². 1,000 years. Fell to corruption, inflation, leaders who forgot the people. Which empire is next?

episodes.title: Enron — The Smartest Guys in the Room

slides.text: Fortune's 'Most Innovative Company' six years running. 7th largest in US. $101 billion revenue. All a lie.
'Mark-to-market' — booked 20 years of future profit in Year 1. Losses in 3,000 shell companies. Financial origami.
Fired bottom 15% every 6 months. Nobody questioned numbers. Questioning meant getting fired.
CEO resigned suddenly. VP Sherron Watkins warned: 'We will implode.' She was right. 4 months.
Dec 2, 2001. Bankruptcy. $74 billion gone. 20,000 jobless. Executives had already sold their shares.
CEO: 24 years prison. 20,000 employees: lost jobs AND retirement. When the house is lies, everyone inside gets hurt. Except the architects.

episodes.synopsis: 'Most Innovative Company' 6 years running. All fake. $74 billion in shareholder value vaporized.
episodes.caption: 'Most Innovative' 6 years. $101 billion revenue. All fake. 20,000 lost everything. Executives cashed out. Who's the next Enron?

episodes.title: The Berlin Wall — An Accidental Freedom

slides.text: 28 years. 155 km of concrete. Guard towers. Shoot-to-kill. 100+ died trying to cross. Fell because of a mistake.
1989. Soviet bloc cracking. Poland free. Hungary opened border. East Germans escaping through other countries.
Nov 9, 1989. 6:53 PM. Spokesman asked when new travel rules start. Hadn't been briefed. 'Immediately.' It was wrong. It changed history.
West German TV broadcast it. Thousands rushed checkpoints. Guards had no orders. One opened the gate. Never ordered to.
Both sides climbed the wall. Strangers hugged. Families reunited after 28 years. Hammers on concrete.
History doesn't always change through wars. Sometimes someone says the wrong thing at the right time.

episodes.synopsis: 28 years of division. Fell because a spokesman said the wrong thing at a press conference.
episodes.caption: 28 years. 100+ deaths. Shoot-to-kill. Fell because a spokesman said the wrong thing. The most beautiful accident in history.

episodes.title: Yahoo — The Company That Said No to Everything

slides.text: 2000. Yahoo WAS the internet. Email, news, search, chat. $125 billion market cap. Google before Google.
1998: Google for $1M — no. 2002: Google for $5B — no. 2006: Facebook for $1B — no. Three nos lost $3 trillion.
7 CEOs in 6 years. Portal → Media → Tech → Media → ???. Didn't know what they were.
3 billion accounts compromised. Didn't disclose for 2 years. Trust: impossible to rebuild.
2017. Verizon buys for $4.5B. WhatsApp sold for $19B. Yahoo — the ENTIRE internet — worth less than a messaging app.
Had every opportunity. Said no to the future three times. Being first doesn't matter if you can't see what's next.

episodes.synopsis: Could've bought Google for $1M. Facebook for $1B. Said no. Sold for less than WhatsApp.
episodes.caption: Could've bought Google for $1M. Facebook for $1B. Said no to both. Sold for less than WhatsApp.

episodes.title: The Titanic — Unsinkable

slides.text: The biggest ship ever. Swimming pool, gym, grand staircase. 2,224 passengers. April 14, 11:40 PM. An iceberg. Marketing doesn't stop physics.
6 iceberg warnings that day. Didn't slow down. 'Unsinkable.' The schedule mattered more than the ocean.
11:40 PM. Scraped starboard. 5 compartments flooded. Designed for 4. Five was death.
Lifeboats for 1,178. Passengers: 2,224. Some launched half-empty — first class wouldn't sit with third class.
2:20 AM. Ship split. Band played 'Nearer, My God, to Thee.' 1,517 died in -2°C water. Most froze.
Sank because they believed their marketing. 'Unsinkable' isn't engineering. It's arrogance.

episodes.synopsis: 6 iceberg warnings ignored. Lifeboats half-empty. 1,517 dead. The band played until the end.
episodes.caption: 6 warnings ignored. Lifeboats half-empty. Band played until the end. 1,517 died because 'unsinkable' was treated as fact.

episodes.title: British India — The Midnight of Freedom

slides.text: 200 years. 400 million subjects. 'Crown Jewel.' They took everything. Then left — after drawing a line.
Cyril Radcliffe. Never been to India. 5 weeks to divide a subcontinent. Pencil through villages, families, temples.
'At the stroke of midnight, India will awake to life and freedom.' Celebration in Delhi. Screaming at the borders.
15 million displaced. 1 million+ killed. Trains arrived with everyone dead. A line by a man who couldn't find Punjab on a map.
And yet — freedom. 200 years ended. The tricolor flew at Red Fort. India was, finally, India's.
Freedom and partition. Joy and genocide. Same day. Some histories don't have heroes. Just survivors.

episodes.synopsis: 400 million freed at midnight. But the same midnight drew a line that killed over a million.
episodes.caption: Freedom at midnight. 400 million freed. 15 million displaced. 1 million killed. August 15: most celebrated and mourned day.

episodes.title: Jet Airways — The Airline That Ran Out of Fuel

slides.text: 124 aircraft. 300+ routes. 16,000 employees. Naresh Goyal built it from one plane. Then couldn't let go.
₹8,500 crore debt. Fuel unpaid. Salaries delayed months. Pilots flying planes the company couldn't maintain.
Banks: 'Step down, we save the airline.' Goyal: No. For months. His ego cost 16,000 livelihoods.
April 17, 2019. Last flight landed 10:30 PM. Pilots in tears. 16,000 found out from TV news.
Planes auctioned. Pilots drove cabs. Goyal arrested 2023. Built India's best airline, destroyed it.
When your identity becomes the company, the company becomes your casualty.

episodes.synopsis: India's best airline. ₹8,500 crore debt. Founder wouldn't step aside. 16,000 jobs lost overnight.
episodes.caption: India's best airline. 124 planes. Killed by debt and ego. Last flight: 10:30 PM. Nobody took off after.

episodes.title: MySpace — Before Facebook Was Cool

slides.text: 2006. 115 million users. More than Google. Your identity was your MySpace profile. Custom HTML. Auto-playing music. Chaos magic.
Murdoch bought for $580M. Then suffocated it with ads. Pop-ups, banners, auto-play everywhere.
Facebook: clean, simple, no sparkly backgrounds. Boring. Boring won. People wanted connection, not decoration.
2009: 10 million users leaving per MONTH. Ghost town with lights still on.
Sold for $35M. Bought for $580M. $545M loss. The social network before Facebook is now a footnote.
Treated users as ad-viewers, not community. When a platform forgets users are people, the exit begins.

episodes.synopsis: 115 million users. Bought for $580M. Sold for $35M. Killed by ads and Facebook.
episodes.caption: 115 million users. $580M → $35M. MySpace had the internet before Facebook. Then filled it with ads. Greed killed it.

episodes.title: The Dinosaurs — 65 Million Years Ago

slides.text: 165 million years. T-Rex. Triceratops. Survived volcanic eruptions, ice ages, continental shifts. Couldn't survive a space rock.
12 km wide. 72,000 km/h. Energy of 10 billion nukes. They didn't see it coming. Nobody sees extinction coming.
Yucatan Peninsula. 180 km crater. 300m tsunamis. Sky caught fire. Burning debris rained globally.
Dust blocked sun for months. Plants died. Herbivores starved. Carnivores lost prey. Age of reptiles ended in cold and dark.
75% of species died. Small mammals survived underground. One of them, 65 million years later, built Instagram.
165 million years. One bad day. Size didn't save them. Adaptability saved the small creatures who became us.

episodes.synopsis: 165 million years of dominance. One asteroid. One bad day. The biggest don't survive. The adaptable do.
episodes.caption: 165 million years. One asteroid. The dinosaurs couldn't adapt. The tiny mammals survived. You exist because they adapted.

episodes.title: Satyam — India's Enron

slides.text: India's 4th largest IT company. 53,000 employees. NYSE-listed. 'Satyam' means truth. Nothing was true.
Inflated revenue by ₹7,000 crore. Faked 13,000 employees. Salaries went to Raju's accounts. 94% of cash didn't exist.
Jan 7, 2009. Raju's confession: 'I inflated balances by ₹5,040 crore.' Compared himself to riding a tiger.
Stock crashed 82% in one day. ₹14,000 crore vaporized. 53,000 learned from TV news.
Raju arrested, sentenced to 7 years. 53,000 served longer — rebuilding careers the fraud destroyed.
'Satyam' = truth. Biggest lie in Indian corporate history wore truth as its name.

episodes.synopsis: 'Satyam' means truth. Chairman faked ₹7,000 crore. 94% of the cash was imaginary. 53,000 employees became collateral.
episodes.caption: 'Satyam' means truth. ₹7,000 crore faked. 94% of cash didn't exist. India's biggest corporate fraud hid behind the most ironic name.

episodes.title: BlackBerry — The Keyboard Graveyard

slides.text: 2008. Every executive, politician, trader had one. 80 million users. 'CrackBerry.' 'Sent from my BlackBerry' was a flex.
BBM was the original WhatsApp. Read receipts, group chats — BlackBerry did it first.
2007. iPhone launches. Co-CEO: 'It can't do what we do.' Right — it couldn't do encrypted emails. Nobody cared.
2011: Global network crashes for 3 days. 2013: Market share drops to 3%. From 50% to 3% in 5 years.
2016: Stops making phones. 2022: OS shuts down. Old BlackBerrys become bricks. Red LED went dark forever.
Thought they were in the email business. Were in the 'pocket computer' business and didn't know it.

episodes.synopsis: 80 million users. Obama's phone. 50% market → 0%. Keyboards met touchscreens.
episodes.caption: 80 million users. Obama's phone. Then 0%. BlackBerry lost to a question it never asked: 'What if people don't want keyboards?'

episodes.title: The Aztec Empire — When Gods Came on Ships

slides.text: Tenochtitlan. Population 200,000. Bigger than London. Causeways, aqueducts, floating gardens. Then 500 strangers arrived.
1519. Cortes with 500 soldiers, 16 horses, cannons. Aztec prophecy said a god would return from the east. Cortes came from the east.
Montezuma could've destroyed them immediately. Instead invited Cortes in. Gave gold. What if he IS a god? That hesitation cost everything.
Smallpox killed 40% of the population. The invisible army deadlier than any cannon.
August 13, 1521. Tenochtitlan fell. Mexico City built on its ruins. Pyramids became church foundations.
The thing that destroys you rarely looks like a threat. It looks like an opportunity.

episodes.synopsis: 200,000 people. Bigger than London. 500 soldiers destroyed a 200-year empire with hesitation and smallpox.
episodes.caption: 200,000 people. Bigger than London. 500 soldiers destroyed it with hesitation, disease, and mistaken identity.

episodes.title: Kingfisher Airlines — The Party That Crashed

slides.text: Red interiors. Designer crew. Every flight a party. Vijay Mallya treated aviation like a nightclub. Nightclubs don't fly.
Never made profit. Not one year. Not one quarter. Lost money every single day of existence.
Salaries delayed months. Fuel cut off. And Mallya was on a yacht in Monaco.
Oct 20, 2012. Last flight. ₹9,000 crore owed. Planes grounded — paint peeling, birds nesting in engines.
2016. Mallya left India. Living in a London mansion. India's most wanted defaulter.
When lifestyle becomes strategy, the party always crashes.

episodes.synopsis: 'Fly the Good Times.' Never made a profit. Not one quarter. ₹9,000 crore debt. Mallya fled.
episodes.caption: Never made profit. Not once. ₹9,000 crore debt. Mallya fled to London. The good times were only for him.

episodes.title: The Ottoman Empire — 600 Years Unraveled

slides.text: 623 years. Three continents. Constantinople, Cairo, Baghdad, Mecca. Longest-lasting empire since Rome.
'Sick Man of Europe.' Lost Greece, Egypt, the Balkans. Shrinking like ice in summer.
1914. Sided with Germany in WWI. Logic: beat Russia. Reality: lost. Catastrophically.
1918. Sykes-Picot. British and French drew lines on maps. Iraq, Syria, Lebanon — borders by Europeans who never walked there.
Nov 1, 1922. Sultanate abolished by vote. Last Sultan fled on a British warship.
Survived 623 years by adapting. Died when it stopped. Sided with the past in a war for the future.

episodes.synopsis: 623 years. Three continents. Abolished by a vote in 1922 after backing the wrong side in WWI.
episodes.caption: 623 years. Abolished by a vote. The Ottoman Empire died from one bad alliance in WWI.

episodes.title: Theranos — The Blood Test That Didn't Work

slides.text: $9 billion. Kissinger on the board. 'Next Steve Jobs.' One drop of blood, 200+ tests. One problem: the tech was a lie.
One drop. 200+ tests. Minutes. No needles. Walgreens signed. Military interested. Investors lined up.
Device failed constantly. Secretly used competitors' machines. Employees threatened with lawsuits for speaking up.
2015. WSJ's John Carreyrou: the device didn't work. Patients had wrong diagnoses. Health at risk.
$9 billion → $0. Holmes found guilty. 11 years in prison. Black turtleneck to prison jumpsuit.
In Silicon Valley, confidence > competence. 'Fake it till you make it' works until someone checks. Always check.

episodes.synopsis: $9 billion for tech that didn't work. Not 'kinda worked.' Didn't. Elizabeth Holmes: 11 years in prison.
episodes.caption: $9 billion for a blood test that didn't work at all. Holmes serving 11 years. Biggest fraud in Silicon Valley.

episodes.title: Indus Valley — The Mystery That Vanished

slides.text: 4,500 years ago. Grid layouts. Indoor plumbing. Standardized bricks across 1,000 km. Sewage when Europe had mud.
Identical bricks everywhere. Trade with Mesopotamia. No weapons found. Peaceful or so powerful nobody dared.
400+ symbols. Nobody's deciphered them in 100 years. Their voice is locked forever.
Around 1900 BCE. Cities abandoned. Not destroyed. People just left. 5 million dispersed.
River dried up? Climate change? Disease? Nobody knows. That's the most haunting part.
Most advanced civilization of its era vanished without a trace. Nothing is permanent.

episodes.synopsis: More advanced than Egypt. Planned cities. 5 million people. Vanished without a trace around 1900 BCE.
episodes.caption: 5 million people. Indoor plumbing 4,500 years ago. Then vanished. No war. No record. History's greatest mystery.

episodes.title: WeWork — The $47 Billion Mirage

slides.text: $47 billion. 'Physical social network.' Co-working valued more than Ford, American Airlines, and Hilton combined.
Business: rent space, subdivide, sublet. That's it. But Neumann called it 'elevating consciousness.' SoftBank: $10 billion.
S-1 dropped. $1.9B losses in 6 months. Neumann trademarked 'We' — charged WeWork $5.9M. $60M private jet.
$47B → $10B → IPO cancelled → fired → $0. All in 6 weeks.
Bankruptcy 2023. Neumann got $1.7B exit. Employees lost jobs. CEO got richer. System working as designed.
Charismatic founder + good story + enough funding = nothing looks like everything. Until someone reads the filing.

episodes.synopsis: A subletting company valued more than Ford. $47 billion → bankruptcy. CEO got $1.7 billion exit package.
episodes.caption: $47 billion. A subletting company. CEO got $1.7B exit. Employees got fired. Most expensive vibes check in history.

episodes.title: Your Last Day — The One Nobody Plans For

slides.text: 24 last days. Kodak ignored digital. Nokia ignored touch. Blockbuster ignored streaming. Rome ignored corruption. All had the information.
Smartest person silenced. 'We've always done it this way.' Growth measured in stories, not numbers. CEO believes their own press.
YOUR career has a Kodak moment coming. The skill you're building — will it matter in 5 years? Are you the Nokia of your office?
Apple almost died 1997. LEGO almost died 2003. Marvel bankrupt 1996. All came back. Someone said 'We need to change. Now.'
When your warning arrives — will you act, or say 'We didn't do anything wrong'?
Every empire has a last day. The ones who survive delay it through change, humility, and listening. Don't be an episode. Be the exception.

episodes.synopsis: 24 episodes. 24 last days. The question isn't IF yours is coming. It's whether you'll see it in time.
episodes.caption: 24 last days. The question isn't IF. It's whether you'll see it in time. What's YOUR warning sign?
